title: The legacy key is withdrawn while the Work Package still asks for an APP story under the legacy title
source: Recovery Workbench Data Migration Stories v3, RWB-DM-001 rows Status, Decision, Withdrawn IDs and Later home; _work/msr/wp/B-P1-06.md story line RWB-P1-DM001-APP; Template and Rules v1 §R5.2 and §R6
section: 1 Story; 2 Business rationale; 7 Acceptance criteria; 19 Out of scope
description: D-RCV-35 (U1) removed the legacy story: Status Removed, Decision D-RCV-35 (U1), Withdrawn IDs 'AC1 to AC3; TC-DM-001-01 to TC-DM-001-04'. The Work Package still lists an APP story under the legacy title 'Migrate account and arrears', with no legacy AC to copy and no legacy test text to carry, and it says nothing about what the story then delivers. Read as written, the slice would have no deliverable; read as a migration, it would contradict the decision that removed the migration.
evidence: Data Migration Stories v3 line 15 'Removed by D-RCV-35. The data is already in ACE.' with the Status, Decision and Withdrawn IDs rows; WP B-P1-06 story line with acs [] and tcs_legacy ['TC-DM-001-01','TC-DM-001-04']
proposed: Keep one APP story per the Work Package and read it as the rework that replaces the migration: the account and arrears read path over the four views and the per-service Flyway version that creates nothing for those rows and records the removal. Keep the legacy title because §R5.2 keeps the legacy compact and title, and correct the title in the next story-master version so that it names the read path, with the story key and the legacy key unchanged.

title: The account and arrears read path is given as a legacy row, not as a deliverable with an answer shape or a cut-off
source: Recovery Workbench Data Migration Stories v3, RWB-DM-001 row 'Read path instead'; FSD P1 v3 A2.3 'What this module does instead' and A2.14; TSD P1 v3 T3.3, T3.4 and T3.7; Template and Rules v1 §R7.3
section: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 8 Business rules; 12 Contract; 13 Solution plan
description: The sources name the four views and the DP01 row, and they name the account read as a path rather than as a story: no source gives the answer shape, the paging, the field order, the not-found behaviour, or the per-source cut-off that marks DP01 late. The freshness rules give the status vocabulary and the message but not the cut-off value, and this story's pattern set holds neither DP-06 nor DP-07, so no parameter or reference read is available to it.
evidence: Legacy row 'Read path instead' names the views only; TSD P1 v3 T3.7 gives 'the source cut-off (configuration, per source)' with no value; FSD P1 v3 A2.14 gates on a complete ACE batch without a cut-off value
proposed: Fix the read as the four views keyed by account_key at the ACE business date, with the answer shaped by the P1 read contract of RWB-P1-E1069-APP and the field order taken from the field IDs, and with the late case answered from v_ace_batch_status and MSG-P1-001 with no parameter read. Revisit only when a per-source cut-off is agreed as a rwb-case parameter.

title: A Day-1 story is tagged wave 4 while its service is wave 1 and the account read is needed by the wave 1 case screens
source: _work/msr/wp/B-P1-06.md story line (wave 4, business_epic EP08, ready Day 1, H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON); Template and Rules v1 §R5.6 and §R5.7; Architecture v5 service table (rwb-source-data wave 1)
description: The Work Package fixes wave 4 and business epic EP08 for this story, and Day 1 readiness on one platform contract. §R5.6 keeps the W-MAP wave only where the business epic is earlier than the service wave; here the W-MAP wave (4) is later than the service wave (1), so the story is tagged wave 4 although its read path is the account source of the wave 1 case screens. The build is not blocked, but the release tag and the date of the read path are not settled by any source.
evidence: WP line: wave 4, business_epic EP08, ready 'Day 1', H ['RWB-PLT-E1044-CON']; §R5.6 wave map EP08 to 4; Architecture v5 service table puts rwb-source-data in wave 1; FSD P1 v3 A2.18 case list reads v_ace_account
proposed: Build from Day 1 as fixed, and release the read path with the wave 1 service deploy, where the P1 read contract and the freshness stamp are live; keep the wave 4 tag as the tag of business epic EP08 and confirm the release date at the wave entry check.

title: The account operation named by the architecture is absent from the TSD P1 endpoint inventory, and the answer field names are in no module specification
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 15 P1 IN and slide 29 (login rwb_source_data); TSD P1 v3 Appendix T-A.1 and T-A.2; Template and Rules v1 §R3 precedence
section: 3 Preconditions; 12.1 REST operations provided; 12.2 REST operations consumed; 12.9 Call-type summary; 13 Solution plan
description: Architecture v5 slide 15 names GET /accounts/{id} in the P1 contract and slide 29 fixes one login, rwb_source_data, with SELECT on the 30 views. TSD P1 v3 Appendix T-A lists API-P1-001 to API-P1-016 and holds no account operation, and neither document gives the answer field names of the account read. The service base /api/recovery/source-data/v1 follows from §R4 and DP-13, so the base is not in doubt, but the operation, its parameters and its answer are.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 lines 1075 and 1114 (P1 IN: REST GET /customers/{id}, /accounts/{id}) and line 2063 (login rwb_source_data); TSD P1 v3 Appendix T-A.1 endpoint inventory; §R4 and DP-13 for the base
proposed: Take the architecture under §R3 (rank 1 over rank 6): the read is answered behind GET /accounts/{id} on /api/recovery/source-data/v1, one hop, 2 s, published by RWB-P1-E1069-APP, and this story adds no path of its own. Add the operation and its answer schema to the next TSD P1 version and to RWB-P1-E1069-CON.

title: The withdrawn migration's file name and its test text are held by no source
source: Recovery Workbench Data Migration Stories v3, RWB-DM-001 row Withdrawn IDs; TSD P1 v3 T3.2 and T3.10; Recovery Workbench Test Cases master
description: The legacy key withdrew TC-DM-001-01 to TC-DM-001-04 and named no migration file, and the withdrawn test text is not in the masters that this run reads. The story therefore cannot assert the absence of a named migration file and cannot copy the withdrawn text: it asserts that no version of the sequence names an extract, a transform, a load or a reconciliation of migrated account or arrears rows, and it keeps the two legacy test case IDs with new Covers.
evidence: Legacy row Withdrawn IDs 'AC1 to AC3; TC-DM-001-01 to TC-DM-001-04'; no migration file name in the legacy section or in TSD P1 v3 T3.2 and T3.10; WP tcs_legacy ['TC-DM-001-01','TC-DM-001-04']
proposed: Keep the two legacy test case IDs with the new Covers and record the full new test in the test case master under the same IDs; do not invent a migration file name, and close this row when the master's next version records the withdrawal.

title: The role RW-CUSTSERV named for this story is held by no source
source: FSD P1 v3 A2.1.3.3, A2.2.3.3 and A2.11.3.3; TSD P1 v3 T6.1; legacy RWB-DM-001 (no permission block); _work/msr/wp/B-P1-06.md prompt line on roles
description: The Work Package names RW-TRIBE, RW-DATASTEW, RW-COE and RW-CUSTSERV as the roles of this story. Three of them are in the sources: the data steward and data product owner, the center of excellence analyst and the squad member. RW-CUSTSERV is in no source read: not in the P1 functional or technical specification, not in the legacy section, and not in the rwb-access role list.
evidence: FSD P1 v3 A2.1.3.3 and A2.2.3.3 name the data steward, the product owner and the center of excellence analyst; TSD P1 v3 T6.1 names RW-DATASTEW; the technical enabler stories name RW-TRIBE; no source holds RW-CUSTSERV
proposed: Use RW-DATASTEW, RW-TRIBE and RW-COE only, as the sources give them. Add RW-CUSTSERV to the story only when a source holds it, as a row of rwb-access (P4).
